name: The Meridian Barge
description:
The Meridian Barge is a decommissioned cargo transport vessel — hull number MW-Φ-1184, originally built in 2161 for bulk freight on the Lake Michigan industrial corridor — that was purchased in 2208 by a consortium of Circuit musicians and converted into a mobile performance venue. The main deck holds a permanent stage and standing room for approximately three hundred and fifty, with a retractable canopy that deploys in poor weather. The hold below has been converted into a secondary acoustic space for intimate sets of sixty, as well as a small recording studio and crew quarters. The Barge runs a scheduled circuit between six dock points across GLMZ's waterfront districts, spending two to four days at each location before moving on.

The Barge's itinerary takes it through Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 waterfront zones, making it one of the few venues in GLMZ that physically travels across tier boundaries. Ticket prices are tiered to location — the Gray Zone dock nights are priced at Φ5-15, Circuit stops at Φ20-50, and the occasional Tier 3 berth at Φ80-150. The same artists perform across all stops, a deliberate programming philosophy that its founding consortium calls 'the same sky for everyone.' The Barge is legally registered as a commercial vessel, which gives it a degree of regulatory ambiguity that has so far insulated it from the venue closure orders that plague the Gray Zone clubs. It has hosted Cassian Pale & The Redline Choir, Okafor & The Driftline, and a legendary unannounced set by Kel Adeyemi-Strand in 2222 that was witnessed by fewer than two hundred people and discussed by thousands.
creator: various
genre: cross-tier, circuit folk, protest, polyrhythmic, acoustic, drift
audience: Cross-tier audiences depending on docking location — the Gray Zone workers at Tier 1 stops, Circuit families at Tier 2 berths, curious Tier 3 professionals when docked north
cultural_impact: The Meridian Barge is the closest thing GLMZ has to a cross-tier cultural institution that was not created by or for corporate interests. Its deliberately sliding price scale and its physical movement through the city's economic geography have made it a visible embodiment of an argument about who music belongs to. Vantablack Media has twice attempted to acquire it or shut it down through maritime regulatory pressure, and twice been rebuffed through a combination of the vessel's ambiguous legal status and a very public community response. The image of the Barge lit up on the lake at night — its stage visible from both the Gray Zone docks and Circuit bridges — has appeared in protest art across the city.
known_fans: circuit workers who follow its schedule
the Gray Zone residents who save for the Φ5 deck tickets
maritime workers who crew adjacent vessels
artists who value the cross-tier audience
story_hooks: Vantablack Media has found a maritime regulation that could impound the Barge permanently at its next Tier 2 dock stop — the consortium has forty-eight hours to find a legal counter, a political ally, or a way to make the Barge disappear into international water jurisdiction before the order is served.

Something was left aboard the Barge after its last the Gray Zone stop — a sealed data chip taped inside the hold's recording studio — and whoever left it has not come back for it, but two different groups of people are now looking for it on the vessel.

A passenger who boarded at a Tier 1 dock stop has not disembarked at any subsequent stop, and the crew has realized the person doesn't appear in any registration log — they simply appeared on deck one night and have been sleeping in the hold ever since, saying nothing, attending every set.
